data.one_liner: Video player plugin and backend APIs supporting desktop and mobile with hardware decoders and FFmpeg.
data.what_it_does: Acts as a backend plugin for the official video_player package and provides a low-level backend player API. Supports hardware-accelerated decoding, optimal rendering APIs across platforms, and most media formats via FFmpeg.
use_when: You need video_player support on desktop platforms like Windows, Linux, and macOS.
You want hardware-accelerated video decoding and optimal rendering performance on mobile and desktop.
You need custom backend player APIs or advanced playback features like snapshots, recording, and custom decoders.
avoid_when: You strictly want a pure Dart audio and video solution without native binary dependencies.
You are using Flutter-snap which sets environment variables that break the C++ compiler build.
strengths: Supports all desktop and mobile platforms with hardware acceleration.
Includes Dolby Vision, custom subtitle, and FFmpeg demuxer support.
Low CPU, GPU, and memory load compared to alternative players.
weaknesses: Requires managing binary SDK dependencies and platform-specific native setups.
Flutter-snap environment variables can break C++ compilation on Linux.
data.setup_notes: Add the package as a direct dependency. For macOS/iOS, clean pod caches if upgrading binary dependencies. For embedded Linux, remove libffmpeg.so.* if using system libraries.

alternatives.name: media_kit
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer a feature-rich media player library built on libmpv instead of libmdk.

alternatives.name: just_audio
alternatives.why_pick_it: If your primary requirement is advanced audio playback and streaming rather than full video capabilities.

alternatives.name: video_player
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you only need the official baseline video playback without cross-desktop hardware acceleration extensions.
